notes: Route: robots.txt (200, permissive, only /wp-admin/ and /wp-includes/ disallowed, Crawl-delay 30, no Sitemap line) -> Yoast sitemap index /sitemap.xml (200) -> post-sitemapN.xml chunks, N in 0..188, ascending N = newest. Fetched chunks from 188 down, parsing <loc> only, until a whole chunk max date < window start (stopped after chunk 186, range 2026-04-24..2026-09-16). Date = /YYYY/MM/DD/ permalink in the URL (the site's own publication date); NOT <lastmod>, which is edit time. Verified on 4 samples (09-30, 10-05, 10-10, 10-20): all 200, 1859-5106 text chars, JSON-LD datePublished exactly equal to listed date. Gotcha that cost two full runs: I built chunk URLs as /post-sitemap<N> without the .xml extension -> every chunk 404; looks exactly like WAF rate-limiting (even the sitemap index still 200 while all sibling URLs 404'd) but was a bug. Fixed by keeping the exact <loc> form; kept a 5s inter-request sleep and one 60s 404-retry as belt-and-braces. Result: 1155 unique URLs, 31/31 days 2026-09-25..2026-10-25, per-day 24..56 (09-30=45, 10-10=26, 10-20=39). ~4 live requests, <1 min runtime. news-sitemap.xml (200, 56 urls, 10-24..10-25 only) and post-sitemap.xml (chunk 0, 2011-12 posts) are NOT useful for this window; /feeds/posts/ is 404.
